the relationship between the SsrA-mediated trans-translation, the DegP-mediated periplasmic protein quality control, and the stress response in the cell.
the role of DegP in the growth of the ssraA mutant at high temperature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the SsrA protein is not required for growth of E. coli at high temperature, but its absence enhances the growth defect of the degP mutant at high temperature, and this is due to the accumulation of polypeptide products of mRNAs programmed by stalled ribosomes.

the ts phenotype of an ssrA-defective degP mutant is due to the accumulation of polypeptide products of truncated mRNAs in the periplasm, and this accumulation is relieved by sigmaE-mediated extracellular stress responses.
